title: Support amortization & breakpoints — scratch calculations
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory sheet to surface how multi-year amortization + support tiers shift the breakeven horizon between on-prem and VPC/private-cloud deployments. Focus is on adding a support amortization line (SLA-weighted premium) and measuring breakpoints under utilization, burst, and license-discount schedules. This is intentionally rough — treat as working scratchpad for product + finance sync.

High-level assumptions (base case):
- Target workload: 100M tokens/day (prod steady-state), 90% generative text, 10% embeddings/rerank.
- Expected steady avg request size: 120 tokens output per request.
- Planning horizon: 36 months for capex amortization.
- On‑prem HW refresh cadence: 3 years; VPC reserved commit: 1–12 month options considered.
- License models: flat per-GPU annual license or per-instance license with volume discounts (tiers at 10, 25, 50 GPUs).
- Support tiers: Standard (8x5, 24h RTO), Business (24x7, 4h RTO), Enterprise (24x7, 1h RTO + on-call escalation). Support uplift expressed as % of license+ops.

Key knobs to vary: utilization (30%–85%), burst buffer reserve (20% of peak), license discount schedule, support uplift %, on‑prem facility costs (power + colocation), networking egress differential for VPC, expected incident minutes per month (to model operational cost credit).

Core formulas (plain text):
- Monthly amortized capex = (HW purchase price + setup + freight + initial kitting) / amortization_months.
- Effective monthly infra cost = monthly amortized capex + colocation_rent_monthly + power_monthly + operational_headcount_allocated_monthly + licensing_monthly.
- Support amortization (SLA-weighted) = support_base_fee_monthly + (incident_minutes_monthly * marginal_incident_cost_per_minute).
- Effective unit cost per 1M tokens = Effective monthly infra cost including support / (expected_tokens_per_month / 1e6).
- Breakeven months vs hosted = (one-time delta in capex + multi-month delta in fixed fees) / monthly savings_vs_hosted.

Worked example table (three scenarios) as CSV rows (columns: scenario, deployment, avg_util_pct, reserved_gpus, monthly_infra_cost_usd, monthly_license_usd, support_tier, support_fee_usd, tokens_per_month, unit_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, breakeven_months_vs_hosted):
observations:
1) Support tier moves effective unit cost materially for low-utilization on‑prem setups — business/enterprise support can exceed license costs when utilization is low.
2) VPC reserved with high utilization and right-sized GPUs closes gap despite higher license per-unit: no capex amortization means breakeven shifts out.
3) A 10% change in avg utilization shifts break-even by ~2–6 months depending on support tier and discount curve.
4) Incident minutes (ops) are asymmetric: enterprise SLAs reduce downtime risk but add predictable premium — map to customer revenue-at-risk to justify uplift.

Sensitivity runs to add next: vary utilization [30,45,60,75,90], vary support uplift [5%,12%,30%], test license discount aggressiveness (no discount, tiered 10/20/30%). Also run a 0–36 month cash-flow table to calculate NPV and IRR for on‑prem vs VPC.

Proposed recommendations (early):
- Introduce an explicit "SLA amortization" line on all customer TCO views: show support absolute $ and support % of total monthly cost. Customers underestimate support when comparing to hosted.
- Provide a single-page "breakeven horizon" visualization for sales: x-axis months, y-axis cost delta vs hosted, toggles for support tier and utilization.
- For Enterprise prospects with high incident sensitivity, prioritize quoting 'support-inclusive' bundles with a capped incident credit schedule to reduce uncertainty.
- Offer an on‑prem financing option (24/36 month) to smooth capex and shorten breakeven for customers with lower utilization.
notes_for_finance: If we present three breakpoints (3, 12, 24 months) show recommended bundle (license+support) that shifts customers into target breakeven. Finance should run NPV @ 8% discount and validate CAPEX accounting treatment for financed hardware. Also capture tax impacts for on‑prem (capital expense) vs VPC (operational expense).
next_steps: Spin a working spreadsheet from this CSV table into product drive (tabbed: base_cases, sensitivity_util, support_uplift, financing_options)
Schedule 30m sync with Solutions Eng + Finance to collect incident marginal cost anchors (target: Dec 10 2025)
Add visualization mockups to product console roadmap ticket
